**Open review checks** (9):

1. (field `domain`) Domain. earth-climate/energy-systems rests on the subdomain's "grid operation" and the family's smart-buildings-challenge example. games-planning's inclusion test (episodes against a responding environment) also fits literally, and the engineering-design scoping survey listed L2RPN as a boundary case with process-control-optimization. Confirm the home.
2. (field `versions`) Identity. The entry is the series, with editions as versions, the NeurIPS 2020 tracks as subsets and Delft 2023 as an event. Grid2Op could be argued a separate benchmark (RL2Grid and others build on it), and the editions differ enough (grid, actions, score) to be entries of their own.
3. (field `versions`) The 2023 Ile-de-France edition is recorded from Grid2Op's docs and Artelys's report alone; its dates, scoring, winners and platform were not read. The survey says the 2023 repeat of the 2022 competition (Delft) was won by another team, with Artelys second, which may be the Delft event rather than the Ile-de-France edition. No edition after 2023 was found. · [S3][l2rpn-s3]
   > The competition of \[33\] was repeated in 2023 \[36\]
4. (field `activity`) activity between-rounds assumes the series may recur; with CodaLab gone and nothing since 2023, closed could be argued if the organisers have ended it. released is null because no source gives the 2019 opening day.
5. (field `capability`) capability. adversarial-robustness and distribution-shift-generalization each rest on one NeurIPS 2020 track (carried as subset capability\_overrides); later environments keep an opponent. planning was rejected because the source does not claim to score plans.
6. (field `data.access`) data.access is private-test-server for the editions' blind rankings, but RTE now provides the 2022 test environment and later papers score on it; whether other editions' test scenarios are public was not established. reproducible\_by\_third\_party false follows the editions, not the post-competition protocol.
7. (field `data.ceiling_anchor_type`) ceiling\_anchor\_type theoretical-maximum takes the normalised score's top of 100; no entrant has come near it (the 20 cost-optimisation points went unclaimed in 2020), and some scenarios may be infeasible. · [S1][l2rpn-s1]
   > But none won those points
8. (field `governance.maintainer_type`) maintainer\_type industry-lab for RTE, a state-owned company; ChaLearn (a nonprofit) co-organises and hosts the site, and Grid2Op has moved to its own GitHub organisation, possibly under another holder.
9. (field `task.scoring`) The 2019 edition scored line margins with a different function and on pypownet; the entry's task and evaluation describe the 2020-on cost-based score. Whether 2019 belongs in the series entry as an edition, rather than as a predecessor, is a judgement.

**Reviewer checklist** for `l2rpn`:

- [ ] Identity and id: the name, aliases, id, paper and release date are right, and this is one benchmark, not a family or an edition of another
- [ ] Domain and capabilities: the primary and secondary subdomains, capabilities, evaluation methods and intended subjects fit, and no rejected term should have been kept
- [ ] Task and evaluation: the task, scoring, ground truth, entrants and harness read as the sources describe them
- [ ] Data and licence: access, refresh, provenance, sizes, subsets, contamination and licences match the sources
- [ ] Governance and independence: maintainer type, submission process, funding and independence flags are right
- [ ] Lifecycle and activity: lifecycle, activity, versions, editions and history are current
- [ ] Every open review check above is answered or resolved
- [ ] Nothing here would embarrass the catalogue in front of a specialist

### 2.10 Smart Buildings Challenge (smart-buildings-challenge)

`data/benchmarks/earth-climate/smart-buildings-challenge.yaml` · `verification_status: ai-drafted-unverified` · curator confidence medium · added 2026-11-04 · last verified 2026-11-18

*A NeurIPS 2026 Kaggle competition: one HVAC control policy, scored in simulation on unseen buildings and climates.*

A NeurIPS 2026 competition, run on Kaggle, for a single HVAC control policy that transfers across commercial buildings. Buildings come from a procedural generator built on an extended version of Google's Smart Buildings Control Suite simulator: two to four floors, varied footprint, room layout and occupancy, six envelope material properties, and air handlers (AHUs) each serving at most ten zones, with a VAV box per zone and one hot-water system. Each building is a Gym-compatible environment. Every five minutes the policy reads an observation whose length depends on the building (zone temperatures and setpoints, AHU and hot-water state, occupancy, outside air temperature, time) and issues a hybrid action whose shape also changes with the building: on/off commands for each AHU and the hot-water system, and continuous setpoints for supply air, static pressure, recirculation, supply water, pump pressure, and each zone's damper and reheat valve. It also receives the building's metadata (floor plan, AHU-to-zone map, action indices, schedule). The per-step reward weights occupant comfort, energy cost and carbon at 0.6, 0.2 and 0.2; all three are penalties, and the comfort term falls without bound beyond 5 K outside the comfort band. Each scenario is a 30-day episode of 8,640 steps, and the score is the mean over scenarios of the magnitude of the mean per-step reward: lower is better, and zero (perfect comfort at no energy or carbon cost) is unreachable. Entrants develop on 6 public buildings under 30 recorded 2023 weather strips from five stations and may generate more buildings; the leaderboard scores 6 unseen buildings at 5 unseen stations (30 scenarios), on a public subset during the competition and on the full private set at the end. Submissions are Kaggle notebooks, re-run without internet against the hidden scenarios. Four hand-written controllers (bang-bang, fixed setpoint, PID, PID with a hot-water reset) ship as a reference range, and there is no learned baseline. A separate paper track awards prizes for write-ups judged on quality and novelty, and the organisers plan to trial winning policies in real buildings after the competition.

#### smart-buildings-challenge · Domain and capabilities

- `domain` = primary earth-climate/energy-systems · [S1][smart-buildings-challenge-s1]
  - why: The scored behaviour is the operation of a building's heating and cooling plant to cut its energy cost and carbon emissions, which is the leaf's "optimising energy ... demand". The family's own examples name smart-buildings-challenge as qualifying ("Building energy optimisation as a real-world control task"), and BuildingsBench, its forecasting neighbour, sits in the same leaf.
  > Building optimization, perhaps more so than any other optimization problem, has enormous potential for Machine Learning (ML) driven impact on climate change
- `capability` = optimization · [S1][smart-buildings-challenge-s1]
  - why: The benchmark states one objective, a fixed weighting of comfort, energy cost and carbon, and ranks policies by how well they optimise it over each episode. The taxonomy names this benchmark as the term's qualifying example.
  > Because the transformation is monotone, minimizing MAE is identical to maximizing the return on every individual scenario.
- `capability` = distribution-shift-generalization · [S1][smart-buildings-challenge-s1]
  - why: Policies are scored only on buildings and weather stations held out from development, with the task, the reward and the generator's parameter ranges unchanged; only the building and its climate move. The source calls this transfer, which the term's test does not decide (the fusion-equilibrium-challenge case).
  > The agent will be evaluated on 6 unseen buildings from the same generator and parameter ranges, at 5 climate stations that appear nowhere in the training set, so the transfer is across both buildings and climates.
- `evaluation_method` = episodic-return · [S1][smart-buildings-challenge-s1]
  - why: The score is the accumulated reward of a control episode in a simulator, every five-minute step of 30 days, divided by the step count and averaged over 30 scenarios. The reward has only penalty terms and the comfort penalty has no floor, so the return is unbounded on the losing side and has no success or partial-credit scale. Its upper bound, zero, is an unreachable ideal rather than a rescaling (see review\_checks).
  > Each scenario runs for 30 days at a 5-minute timestep and every step is scored
- `designed_for_subjects` = rl-policy, classical-algorithm · [S1][smart-buildings-challenge-s1]
  - why: Each building is a Gym-compatible reinforcement learning environment, built for trained control policies. Four hand-written controllers (bang-bang, fixed setpoint, PID and PID with a hot-water reset) are scored beside an entrant's policy as its reference range, which the classical-algorithm test admits for baselines; they do not enter the leaderboard metric. Public notebooks on Kaggle enter both kinds.
  > Each building is exposed as a Gym-compatible RL environment.
- `evaluation_target` = learned-system · [S7][smart-buildings-challenge-s7]
  - why: The hand-written controllers are a reference range, not the subject; the competition asks for a learned building foundation model.
  > There is no learned baseline. Bring your own.

Considered and rejected:

- `domain` not `engineering-design/process-control-optimization` · [S2][smart-buildings-challenge-s2]
  - why: The leaf's definition, controlling or optimising a process against operating objectives, fits the act, but its family's exclusion test sends a system that is operated rather than designed elsewhere, and the family names this benchmark as its near miss ("the scored act is operating a building's energy system, not designing one"). The engineering-design scoping survey flagged building and grid control as this leaf's open boundary with energy-systems; l2rpn takes the same reading (see review\_checks).
  > You are \*\*not\*\* predicting labels, and there is no test CSV.
- `capability` not `transfer-learning` · [S4][smart-buildings-challenge-s4]
  - why: The objective and the reward are the same on every building, and the held-out buildings come from the same generator and ranges, so by both terms' tests the move is a shift of inputs. The one argument the other way is that the observation and action vectors change shape per building, which could be read as a new embodiment (see review\_checks).
  > both the observation and action vectors change shape per building, and there is no fixed input or output mapping the policy can memorize
- `capability` not `scientific-prediction` · [S2][smart-buildings-challenge-s2]
  - why: Nothing is predicted against a reference; the Kaggle page says so in as many words.
  > You are \*\*not\*\* predicting labels, and there is no test CSV.
- `capability` not `sample-efficiency` · [S1][smart-buildings-challenge-s1]
  - why: No budget is fixed; entrants may generate as many training buildings as they like.
  > Organizers can sample fresh evaluation buildings to defeat memorization
- `evaluation_method` not `simulation-rollout` · [S1][smart-buildings-challenge-s1]
  - why: The episodes are simulated, but each is scored as accumulated reward, not as success, the fraction of goals met or efficiency under a cap; the term's exclusion sends unbounded cumulative reward to episodic-return. Both terms resolve the same comparability profile with these subjects.
  > the drop is linear up to 5 K outside the band and quadratic and unbounded beyond, so abandoning comfort is never free
- `evaluation_method` not `statistical-fit` · [S5][smart-buildings-challenge-s5]
  - why: Kaggle labels the metric mean absolute error, but the target is the constant zero, so it is the magnitude of the mean per-step reward; no prediction is compared with an observation.
  > "leaderboardPercentage":33
- `evaluation_method` not `expert-panel-assessment` · [S2][smart-buildings-challenge-s2]
  - why: The paper track's prizes are judged on quality, novelty and clarity, but they rank write-ups, not the policies; the benchmark's score is the leaderboard's.
  > Paper prizes are not based on the metric alone, but on overall quality and novelty of the method, and writing clarity.
- `designed_for_subjects` not `domain-specialist-model` · [S1][smart-buildings-challenge-s1]
  - why: The proposal asks whether domain-specific models or generic foundation models will win, but names no model class it is built for; the starter kit ships no learned baseline.
  > whether domain specific models will win out\[19\], or whether generic foundation models will generalize best.
- `designed_for_subjects` not `agent-scaffold` · [S2][smart-buildings-challenge-s2]
  - why: A notebook may load public pretrained models, including language models, but it runs with no internet and acts through get\_action every step; nothing in the sources designs for a prompted agent, and such an entrant would be a claim-level subject.
  > Internet access disabled
- `designed_for_subjects` not `physical-robot-system` · [S1][smart-buildings-challenge-s1]
  - why: The organisers plan live trials of winning policies in real buildings after the competition, but no score comes from hardware.
  > We will use a simulated environment for the contest, and will evaluate winning solutions on real buildings after the contest ends.

**Open review checks** (13):

1. (field `execution.harness`) The simulator's reward changed on 2026-11-16 (starter-kit pull requests 2 and 3, the tank energy balance and airflow-weighted return air), after the Round One deadline and before the final one. Whether Kaggle's gateway was updated, whether the public leaderboard was re-scored or now mixes scores from two simulator revisions, and which commit the final re-run of the top 7 policies fixes, are not stated; the competition's discussion and overview pages render by script and were not read. · [S8][smart-buildings-challenge-s8]
   > Legitimate policies can shift a few percent, so merging means re-scoring.
2. (field `domain`) Placement. The taxonomy names this benchmark as an earth-climate example, and energy-systems reads "optimising energy ... demand", but the family's inclusion test asks for energy "in a geophysical setting" and its exclusion sends a physical process outside an Earth-system context to physics. engineering-design/process-control-optimization fits the act by its definition and is rejected only through its family's operated-not-designed exclusion. A building's HVAC plant is the stress case the recon note flagged; the entry follows the taxonomy's examples, as l2rpn does.
3. (field `evaluation_method`) episodic-return or simulation-rollout. The score is accumulated reward with no floor (the comfort penalty is unbounded), which is episodic-return, but the reward is bounded above by zero, and episodic-return's inclusion speaks of "no defined maximum". ceiling\_anchor\_type is theoretical-maximum on the same bound. Both methods resolve the simulation profile here, so only the facet and saturation handling change. · [S1][smart-buildings-challenge-s1]
   > The reward is bounded above by zero.
4. (field `capability`) distribution-shift-generalization rather than transfer-learning. The task and reward are fixed and the buildings come from the same generator, but the observation and action spaces change shape per building, which a reviewer may read as a new embodiment and so transfer-learning. · [S4][smart-buildings-challenge-s4]
   > Across the 6 training buildings, K runs from 3 to 9 and V from 28 to 85, so the discrete space spans 4 to 10 bits and the continuous space 67 to 199 values.
5. (field `capability`) No capability term covers closed-loop control of a non-embodied physical plant; sensorimotor-control is defined for a body. Logged with bench tag-gap (proposed plant-control).
6. (field `governance.funding`) Prize split. The proposal gives $2K for Round One and $38K for the final deadline; the site and Kaggle give $25,000 for the leaderboard and $15,000 for the paper track. The entry follows the competition pages. · [S1][smart-buildings-challenge-s1]
   > Round One deadline (NeurIPS poster; $2K in prizes) Paris Workshop Final deadline ($38K in prizes)
7. (field `governance.submission_process`) Team size and submission form. The proposal allows teams of up to four and an Entry of a module, weights and a reproducibility bundle; Kaggle's rules allow five and take a notebook only. · [S2][smart-buildings-challenge-s2]
   > The maximum Team size is five (5).
8. (field `activity`) Final deadline time. Kaggle's timeline says every deadline is at 23:59 UTC, but its record holds 17:59:59 UTC on 2027-01-15. · [S2][smart-buildings-challenge-s2]
   > All deadlines are at 11:59 PM UTC on the corresponding day unless otherwise noted.
9. (field `governance.known_limitation`) Real-building trials. The proposal invites top teams to live trials at four physical partner sites; Kaggle's description says three real buildings. Neither is scored, and no date is given. · [S2][smart-buildings-challenge-s2]
   > Winning solutions may have the opportunity to test their models on three real buildings.
10. (field `learned_entrant_evidence`) learned\_entrant\_evidence is a public notebook whose title names residual PPO; its code was not read, the organisers ship no learned baseline, and many of the top public notebooks are PI or rule-based controllers. The leaderboard was not read because its rows name participants.
11. (field `governance.maintainer_type`) maintainer\_type academic-lab rests on Kaggle naming the University of Washington host and sponsor; the organisers span five universities, Mila and four companies, and the code sits in a dedicated account with no stated institution, which community-collective's test may fit better.
12. (field `lineage`) The reward differs from the Smart Buildings Control Suite's 3C reward, which is bounded in \[-1, 0\]; the challenge's comfort term is unbounded and occupancy-weighted. Whether the suite itself (a 2024-2025 benchmark of 11 real buildings) deserves an entry, with this challenge linked to it, is open; lineage is not recorded. · [S9][smart-buildings-challenge-s9]
   > formulated as an approximate regret function, bounded in the range \[-1,0\]
13. (field `release_venue`) The NeurIPS blog's competition-track post (src-neurips-2026-competitions-blog, on main) lists the challenge, but its extract has no window on that line, so release\_venue cites the site instead.

**Reviewer checklist** for `smart-buildings-challenge`:

- [ ] Identity and id: the name, aliases, id, paper and release date are right, and this is one benchmark, not a family or an edition of another
- [ ] Domain and capabilities: the primary and secondary subdomains, capabilities, evaluation methods and intended subjects fit, and no rejected term should have been kept
- [ ] Task and evaluation: the task, scoring, ground truth, entrants and harness read as the sources describe them
- [ ] Data and licence: access, refresh, provenance, sizes, subsets, contamination and licences match the sources
- [ ] Governance and independence: maintainer type, submission process, funding and independence flags are right
- [ ] Lifecycle and activity: lifecycle, activity, versions, editions and history are current
- [ ] Every open review check above is answered or resolved
- [ ] Nothing here would embarrass the catalogue in front of a specialist
